body:
P4-24, two more open questions for the code step (found after the drawing; the drawing does not decide them).

(1) The quality "Compatible" (MP3 192 kbps, domain/audio_quality.dart, rank 70, offered in the "On mobile data" picker) is the format for a device or car that cannot play Opus. "Cap at Data saver (Opus 48)" would switch such a person to a format their device may not play. Proposed for the advisor: the cap keeps the person's FORMAT family (a Compatible choice is capped to a low-bitrate MP3 of the same family, or Data saver is not applied to it), never the codec chosen by us; this needs the server's transcoder to offer a low-bitrate MP3 (check stream?format=mp3&maxBitRate=). Until decided, the code must not hand Opus to a Compatible listener.

(2) The grey note "Only used on mobile data. You're on Wi-Fi, so nothing is limited now." is drawn for Wi-Fi only. What is shown on Ethernet, on a VPN-only link or with no connection at all is not drawn: the code step should show no note there (or the plain truth), and the derived value "Data saver is in force" must be false there (only a mobile link makes it true).

Also drawn on purpose: the "Data saver is limiting this" line (Playback "On mobile data" row, Downloads "Quality" line) appears only when the person's own choice is above Data saver (rank 40); when it already is Data saver, nothing is limited and nothing is said.
